weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Average enterprise shipper spends approximately $5.1 million annually on LTL-related damage and loss issues in 2024; LTL damage rate of 1.24% (1 in 80 shipments); average cost $1,796 per claim
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Single-trade-source: synchrogistics.com is an LTL tech vendor maintaining its own claims index; flockfreight.com is a competing LTL carrier blog. Both are vendor-adjacent secondary sources. No government statistics, industry association survey, or audited carrier filing anchors the 1.24% damage rate or the $5.1M average cost figure.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search ATA (American Trucking Associations) annual freight statistics for LTL damage rates. Also check NMFTA (National Motor Freight Traffic Association) claims data and TIA (Transportation Intermediaries Association) annual survey. Search query: 'LTL freight damage rate 2024 ATA NMFTA industry survey' and 'freight claim statistics annual report 2024 transportation intermediaries association'.

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Strategic cargo theft (fictitious pickups, double brokering, identity theft) rose 1,475% between 2022 and 2024, now representing approximately 40% of all cargo crime, with an average carrier loss of $520,000 per incident
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Trade press (truckinginfo) plus vendor marketing (travelers.com is an insurer's resource page). The 1,475% statistic is extraordinary and its original primary source is not identified — it may trace back to CargoNet or a private intelligence firm's estimate. travelers.com is auto-low-vendor (insurer marketing). No primary-association or government source cited.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Locate the primary source of the 1,475% figure. CargoNet (Verisk) publishes annual strategic theft reports — search 'CargoNet strategic cargo theft 2024 annual report fictitious pickup statistics'. Also check FMCSA enforcement data for double-brokering enforcement actions (government source). Alternatively, NICB publishes cargo crime trend data. Search: 'NICB strategic cargo theft 2024 fictitious pickup double brokering statistics'.

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: The global secure logistics market (armored transport, escorts, cash-in-transit) was valued at approximately $85.2 billion in 2023 — of which transportation accounted for 71% of market share
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Auto-downgrade aggregator (Fortune Business Insights). The $85.2B market size is the only quantitative anchor for the scale of the global escort and secure logistics market in PP 5.3. It is used to establish that physical security services are a 'major ongoing cost' — a load-bearing claim for the pain point's severity. No primary filing or industry association source cross-validates this figure. The Brink's 10-K ($5B revenue) and Securitas Annual Report ($15.3B) are already cited elsewhere but don't directly validate a $85.2B total market.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Use the Brink's 10-K segment data (CVS/BGS revenue) and Securitas guarding revenue breakdown plus Allied Universal and GardaWorld estimated revenues to construct a bottom-up market estimate from primary filings. Also search ASIS International (security industry association) annual security market report for global secure transport market sizing. Search query: 'ASIS International security industry market size 2024 global armored transport cash-in-transit'. Alternatively, check if IBIS World or IBISWorld has a publicly summarized secure logistics market report excerpt that can be cross-validated.

gate_reasoning: 82.2% of claims in Stage 5 score Low confidence, driven primarily by pervasive vendor-marketing override (31 claims), aggregator market research auto-downgrade (17 claims), and 15 ASSUMED-tagged claims with no source corroboration. The corpus is not structurally empty — TT Club/BSI and TAPA EMEA anchor the cargo theft severity claims solidly (11 High-confidence claims), and the Brink's and Securitas filings provide credible revenue anchors. However, the three most important pain-point cost anchors (PP 5.1 LTL damage rate, PP 5.2 strategic theft growth rate, PP 5.3 escort market size) all score Low due to vendor-adjacent or aggregator sourcing. Deep research targeting these three claims plus attended fetches for the BSI/TT Club 2024 PDF (marked [NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH]) would materially improve the corpus. The 5 ASSUMED escort pricing claims (ASSUMED-1 through ASSUMED-5 in value-chain; ASSUMED-2, ASSUMED-3 in pain-points) are inherent field-validation gaps that cannot be resolved from web research alone. Ship with re-run on the top 3 weak claims before final gate.
